The DEXA-PSYCH trial is an investigator-initiated, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel
group superiority trial. Three-hundred participants meeting criteria for moderate-to-severe depression were 
randomized in a 1:1 ratio to 1 week of either dexamethasone or placebo as add-on treatment to treatment as usual.

**Sponsor Institution:** [Copenhagen Research Centre for Biological and Precision Psychiatry](https://research.regionh.dk/en/organisations/copenhagen-research-centre-for-biological-and-precision-psychiatr/), Mental Health Centre Copenhagen, Copenhagen University Hospital---Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg, Copenhagen, Denmark.

**Sponsor and Principal Investigator:**  [Michael Eriksen Benros](about.qmd#sponsor-and-principal-investigator).

## Status

Per date: 2026-11-08

- **Enrollment:** Done. 300 participants randomized.
- **Completion:** Main trial (up to day 28 visit) is complete. Six-month follow-up is on-going.

For further details, see [the timeline](#sec-timeline).

## Background

Depression is one of the leading causes of years lived with disability, globally. The effects 
of current pharmacological treatments are small-to-moderate and often delayed by weeks. Immunological
disturbances have been associated with depression and meta-analyses have suggested that anti-inflammatory agents have moderate-to-large anti-depressant effects. 
The largest effects were reported for glucocorticoids. However, previous trials were too small to legitimize standard use of glucocorticoids as add-on treatment in depression. 


## Purpose

The purpose of the DEXA-PSYCH trial was to investigate the effect and safety of short-term, oral dexamethasone compared to placebo as add-on therapy in moderate-to-severe depression.

The primary publication of the DEXA-PSYCH trial is available [here]() (Link will go live upon publication of the primary paper.) For more information on publications see [here](publications.qmd).


## Protocol and Trial registration

The DEXA-PSYCH trial has EU Trial registration number [2022-501428-45-00](https://euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public/view/2022-501428-45-00?lang=en) with WHO universal Trial Identifier U1111-1280-7614.

The Trial protocol is available [here](https://euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public/view/2022-501428-45-00?lang=en) in its latest version and an earlier version is presented in [Rømer et al (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13063-025-08989-2).


## Statistical Analysis Plan

The Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) was archived and locked in a persistent and immutable [Zenodo DOI](`r sap_doi`) prior to unblinding of the randomization list. The time of unblinding coincides with locking of the database and is called *database lock* (DBL).


## Analysis code

All code to produce the statistical analyses is openly shared on the [DEXA-PSYCH GitHub repository](https://github.com/Biological-and-Precision-Psychiatry/DEXA-PSYCH). 

Analyses were programmed with dummy treatment-group identifiers, and the code was archived before unblinding. 
The primary analysis of the primary endpoint was independently parallel programmed by two separate statisticians.

The [README file](https://github.com/Biological-and-Precision-Psychiatry/DEXA-PSYCH/blob/main/README.md) describes the structure and contents of the code base.

The [Change log](https://github.com/Biological-and-Precision-Psychiatry/DEXA-PSYCH/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) describes the evolution and maintenance of the code base and new releases of trial results.


## Timeline {#sec-timeline}

The key timeline for the main trial is as follows:

- 2021-12-09: Grant awarded from [the Novo Nordisk Foundation](https://novonordiskfonden.dk/en/)
- 2022-07-25: Pre-registration on [the EU Clinical Trials Information System](https://euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public/view/2022-501428-45-00?lang=en) and submission for authority approval
- 2022-10-21: Approval granted by [the Danish Medicines Agency](https://laegemiddelstyrelsen.dk/en/) and [the Danish Health Research Ethics Committee](https://www.regionh.dk/til-fagfolk/Forskning-og-innovation/De-regionale-videnskabsetiske-komiteer/Sider/default.aspx?rhKeywords=De+videnskabsetiske+komiteer)
- 2022-12-28: Recruitment initiated
- 2023-01-13: First patient randomized
- 2026-04-16: Last version of the protocol (version 1.4) approved by the authorities and  [published](https://euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public/view/2022-501428-45-00?lang=en)
- 2026-10-12: Day-28 visit of the last patient
- 2026-10-19: Final external monitoring by [the Good Clinical Practice (GCP) unit](https://gcp-enhed.dk/english/)
- 2026-10-20: Statistical analysis plan locked in [Zenodo DOI](`r sap_doi`)
- 2026-10-21: Database locked, Statistical analysis code finalized and locked in [Zenodo DOI](`r code_doi`)
- 2026-10-22: Randomization list received: unblinding of statisticians, principal investigator and selected sub-investigators
- 2026-10-23: All Pre-specified analyses run and results archived in [Zenodo DOI](`r tlf_pp_doi`) and post-unblinding code
archived in [Zenodo DOI](`r code_doi_post`)
- 2026-mm-dd: Primary publication published


As of October 2026 three assessors remain unblinded to collect 6-month follow-up data. The last follow-up data is expected to be collected March 2027.

A [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/) archive is a time-stamped, and immutable snapshot of a research output (such as software, data, or publications) stored in Zenodo and assigned a DOI (Digital Object Identifier) for permanent reference.
